title: Isosceles-free sets in the body-centred cubic crystal
statement: Let the body-centred cubic crystal B_N be the points (x, y, z) with 0 <= x, y, z <= 2N - 2 whose coordinates are all even (the N^3 corners of an (N-1) x (N-1) x (N-1) block of cubes of edge 2) or all odd (the (N-1)^3 cube centres); squared distance dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2, nearest neighbours at squared distance 3. Determine the largest number of points of the body-centred cubic crystal B_N such that no point is equidistant from two others (no isosceles triangle, flat ones included: no point is the midpoint of two others), as a function of N. The exact values are known (ours) for N <= 3; the headline cell is N = 5: find 15 or more such points of the region of side 5 (an upper bound is 47).
submission: Text file: one point 'x y z' per line, a point of the region of side 5 (lines starting with # are ignored).
score: the number of points (larger is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: 14 points of the region of side 5 with no point equidistant from two others (no isosceles triangle, flat ones included), the best set CP-SAT found in 10 seconds, started from the set for side N - 1 (tools/lattice_sets.py)

context: A set of points is isosceles-free when no point of it is equidistant from two others: no three of its points form an isosceles triangle, counting the flat case of a point midway between two others. For the n x n square grid the largest such sets have become a test bed for machine-assisted constructions: PatternBoost (Charton, Ellenberg, Wagner and Williamson, 2024) and AlphaEvolve (Georgiev, Gomez-Serrano, Tao and Wagner, 2025) found sets of 108 to 112 points in the 64 x 64 grid, the first values are OEIS A271907, and the best lower bound proved, of order n sqrt(log log n / log n) (arXiv:2610.04194, 2026), is far from the subquadratic upper bounds (the grid question is Erdos problem #1207). The body-centred cubic crystal (iron, tungsten, the alkali metals) gives each site 8 nearest neighbours at the surrounding cube corners or centres and 6 next-nearest along the axes, so equal distances abound. How fast the largest isosceles-free sets grow is open.
references: F. Charton, J. S. Ellenberg, A. Z. Wagner, G. Williamson, PatternBoost: constructions in mathematics with a little help from AI, arXiv:2411.00566 (2024)
B. Georgiev, J. Gomez-Serrano, T. Tao, A. Z. Wagner, Mathematical exploration and discovery at scale, arXiv:2511.02864 (2025)
Sparse coloring for isosceles-free grids: an AI-assisted proof case study, arXiv:2610.04194 (2026)
OEIS A271907 (largest subsets of the n x n grid with no isosceles triangle)

novelty.verdict: new question for this lattice: isosceles-free subsets are studied for the n x n square grid (OEIS A271907, PatternBoost, AlphaEvolve, arXiv:2610.04194); no result was found for the body-centred cubic crystal, and it is not in the OEIS by name (too few exact values are known to search by terms).
closest: The n x n square grid (OEIS A271907; PatternBoost arXiv:2411.00566; AlphaEvolve arXiv:2511.02864; arXiv:2610.04194): the same question in another lattice.
Erdos-type questions on isosceles sets in the plane and in space: point sets in which every three points form an isosceles triangle, the opposite extreme.

baseline.text: 14 for N = 5, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: the points in `refs/bcc-isosceles.txt` (the best set CP-SAT found in 10 seconds, started from the set for side N - 1 (tools/lattice_sets.py)). Exact values for N = 2..3: 4, 8 (CP-SAT (OR-Tools 9.15, one worker) proved the optimum of the 0/1 model in tools/lattice_sets.py). Upper bound for N = 5: 47 (every chosen point sees the others at different distances, and no point of the region sees more than 46 different distances).
